gap: No result ChatGPT got says that running the Wuben X5 on its four-AAA backup drops Turbo from 1,300 lm to 850 lm. The AAA cells go straight into the battery bay behind a rear panel (Wuben ships no holder), and a reviewer ran it on Eneloop NiMH cells.
standout_why: I compared against our current dealectric.com page, which I opened. It says 'four AAA cells run all three lights' but gives no output on AAA and doesn't say whether an adapter is needed. Both ChatGPT answers only say 'replaceable battery and AAA backup compatibility' and give no limits. I could not open the cited rival pages: Popular Mechanics (ArkPro Ultra review), Lowe's (Klein) and Yahoo Tech (the 'flashlight of the future' test) all refused the fetch with 403 errors. So I can't rule out that one of them mentions AAA output. Those pages cover Olight and Klein lights, which have sealed batteries, so the X5's AAA behavior is unlikely to be there.
decides: It supports the X5 as the pick for 'replaceable battery / works off store batteries'. Our page now has to say the AAA fallback is a reduced mode (850 lm Turbo instead of 1,300 lm). It also strengthens the contrast with the Olight ArkPro: its 2,000 mAh battery is built in, charges only by USB-C or Olight's magnetic MCC cable, and 1Lumen says the light won't work out of the box until it's been on a charger. The Class 3R X5 is limited to certain countries (a BLF reviewer quotes Wuben: US and Canada), so buyers elsewhere get the Class 1 version.

findings.label: White-light output on AAA vs Li-ion pack
findings.value: AAA: Turbo 850→400 lm (1 min + 1 h), High 350 lm 2 h, Medium 150 lm 5 h, Low 50 lm 15 h, Eco 1 lm 200 h. Li-ion pack: Turbo 1,300→400 lm
findings.source_title: Wuben X5: Why Replaceable Batteries Matter for EDC (Wuben blog)
findings.note: From the maker's own runtime table. Only Turbo is lower on AAA (850 vs 1,300 lm). Wuben says AAA keeps 'the same practical runtime across most brightness levels'. The table doesn't say which AAA chemistry it used.

findings.label: AAA backup: cell count and fitting
findings.value: 4 × AAA, inserted directly through a rear flip-open panel. Reviewer ran it on Eneloop NiMH, and all three lights still worked, 'slightly dimmer'
findings.note: No holder or adapter is mentioned. roma58's BLF review (2026-06-10) says a silkscreen under the rear buttons shows which way the AAA cells go.

findings.label: Rechargeable pack and charging
findings.value: ABN1200 Li-ion, 1,200 mAh / 4.44 Wh, removable. USB-C input 5 V/1.2 A, about 1.5 h per the manual (measured 1 h 20 min on a 5 V/2 A adapter, 1.2 A max). Light runs while charging except High and Turbo white
findings.note: Box listed: X5 with clip and battery installed, Type-C charging cord, H1.5 hex wrench, manual. No AAA holder in the box.

findings.label: Battery and charging compatibility
findings.value: 2,000 mAh built-in LiPo, not replaceable. Charges by USB-C port (C-to-C works) or Olight's proprietary MCC magnetic tail cable (MCC 1 A cable in box). Olight specifies about 1.5 h on USB-C and about 3 h on MCC; measured 1 h 36 min at about 7 W. Ships locked and won't work until connected to a charger
findings.note: 1Lumen lists the box as ArkPro, MCC cable, manual and UV card, with no dock or cradle. Laser listed as green about 520 nm, Class 3R, but 1Lumen's own figures conflict (3 or 5 mW).
